service:
Lambda

Overview

Lambda Core is a set of APIs for managing shared infrastructure resources used by Lambda. The Lambda Core API provides operations for:

  1. Creating and managing network connectors that enable Lambda MicroVMs and Lambda Web Functions to access resources in your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC).

  2. Creating customer-managed runtimes which can be used with Lambda Event Functions.

Network connectors provision elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in your VPC subnets, providing a managed network path from Lambda compute environments to private resources such as Amazon RDS databases, Amazon ElastiCache clusters, and internal APIs. You create a network connector once and attach it to one or more Lambda MicroVMs or Lambda Web Functions at run time.

A customer-managed runtime is a Lambda runtime that you create and manage as a standalone resource. Lambda Event Functions can use your customer-managed runtime instead of using one of the built-in Lambda-managed runtimes. Customer-managed runtimes enable you to create customized runtimes for your workloads, and give you control over runtime updates and the deprecation lifecycle.

The Lambda Core API Reference provides information about each of the API methods, including details about the parameters in each API request and response.

You can use Software Development Kits (SDKs), Integrated Development Environment (IDE) Toolkits, and command line tools to access the API. For installation instructions, see Tools for Amazon Web Services.

For a list of Region-specific endpoints that Lambda supports, see Lambda endpoints and quotas in the Amazon Web Services General Reference.

When making the API calls, you will need to authenticate your request by providing a signature. Lambda supports signature version 4. For more information, see Signature Version 4 signing process in the Amazon Web Services General Reference.

operations.CreateNetworkConnector:
Creates a network connector that enables Lambda compute resources to route outbound traffic through your Amazon VPC. The network connector provisions elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in the subnets you specify, providing a managed network path to private resources such as databases, caches, and internal APIs.

This operation is asynchronous. The network connector starts in PENDING state while ENIs are provisioned in your VPC (provisioning typically takes up to 10 minutes). Use GetNetworkConnector to poll the connector state until it reaches ACTIVE. Once active, you can attach the connector to supported Lambda compute resources — such as MicroVMs and WebFunctions — at run time. For how to attach a connector, see the documentation for the specific compute type.

This operation is idempotent when you provide a ClientToken — if you retry a request that completed successfully using the same client token, the operation returns the existing connector without creating a duplicate.
operations.CreateRuntime: Creates a customer-managed runtime, a resource providing a centrally managed execution environment for your Lambda functions. The runtime resource is the parent of the runtime version and runtime alias child resources.
operations.CreateRuntimeAlias: Creates a new customer-managed runtime alias. The alias is a named pointer to a runtime version. Functions consume the customer-managed runtime through the runtime alias.
operations.CreateRuntimeVersion: Creates a new runtime version. A runtime version defines the function execution environment by referencing a container image. Runtime versions are immutable. To update the runtime, create a new runtime version and migrate functions by updating the runtime aliases to point to the new runtime version.
operations.DeleteNetworkConnector:
Initiates deletion of a network connector. The connector transitions to DELETING state while elastic network interfaces are cleaned up asynchronously. After deletion completes, subsequent calls to GetNetworkConnector return ResourceNotFoundException.

This operation is idempotent — calling delete on a connector that is already deleting or has been deleted succeeds without error. You can delete connectors in ACTIVE or FAILED states. Before deleting a connector, ensure that no Lambda compute resources are using it, as they will lose VPC egress connectivity immediately.

Deleting with an unqualified identifier removes the connector and all of its versions. To remove a single historical version, supply its version-qualified ARN; the connector and its remaining versions are unaffected. You can't delete the latest version on its own — delete the connector to remove it.
operations.DeleteRuntime: Schedules a customer-managed runtime to be deleted. Runtimes scheduled for deletion enter the PENDING_DELETION state and can be restored during the scheduled deletion window. Runtime versions and aliases must be deleted or scheduled for deletion before deleting the runtime. Function invokes fail for functions using runtime versions or aliases that are deleted or pending deletion.
operations.DeleteRuntimeAlias: Schedules a runtime alias to be deleted. Runtime aliases scheduled for deletion enter the PENDING_DELETION state and can be restored during the scheduled deletion window. Function invokes fail for functions using runtime aliases that are deleted or pending deletion.
operations.DeleteRuntimeVersion: Schedules a runtime version to be deleted. Runtime versions scheduled for deletion enter the PENDING_DELETION state and can be restored during the scheduled deletion window. Function invokes fail for functions using a runtime version that is deleted or pending deletion.
operations.GetNetworkConnector:
Retrieves the current configuration, state, and metadata of a network connector. The Identifier parameter accepts the connector ID, name, or full ARN. Use this operation to poll connector state after creation or update, or to inspect the current VPC configuration and any failure reasons.

The response includes the full connector configuration, current state, and — if the connector has been updated — the LastUpdateStatus and LastUpdateStatusReasonCode fields that indicate whether the most recent update succeeded or failed.
operations.GetRuntime: Retrieves the configuration and metadata of a runtime.
operations.GetRuntimeAlias: Retrieves the configuration, state, and metadata of a runtime alias.
operations.GetRuntimeVersion: Retrieves the configuration, state, and metadata of a runtime version.
operations.ListNetworkConnectorVersions:
Returns a paginated list of the versions of a network connector. Each configuration update creates a new immutable version; this operation lists those versions for the connector you specify. You can optionally filter results by version state. Use the Marker parameter from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results.

Each item in the response includes the version-qualified ARN, version number, current state, and last modified timestamp for that version. To retrieve the current (latest) configuration of the connector, use GetNetworkConnector; to inspect a specific version, call GetNetworkConnector with a version-qualified identifier.
operations.ListNetworkConnectors:
Returns a paginated list of network connectors in your account for the current Region. You can optionally filter results by connector state. Use the Marker parameter from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results.

Each item in the response includes the connector ARN, name, ID, type, current state, and last modified timestamp. To retrieve full configuration details for a specific connector, use GetNetworkConnector.
operations.ListRuntimeAliases: Returns a paginated list of aliases for the specified runtime.
operations.ListRuntimeVersions: Returns a paginated list of versions for the specified runtime.
operations.ListRuntimes: Returns a paginated list of runtimes in your account for the current Region.
operations.RestoreRuntime: Cancels a pending scheduled deletion, returning the resource to the ACTIVE state. Scope is determined by the RuntimeName path parameter plus an optional, mutually exclusive RuntimeVersion or RuntimeAlias query parameter: with neither, the runtime itself is restored; with RuntimeVersion, the named runtime version; with RuntimeAlias, the named runtime alias. Restoring a resource that is already ACTIVE is a no-op success. Restore only works while the target is PENDING_DELETION; once the scheduled deletion has begun executing (DELETING) or has completed, the call fails.
operations.UpdateNetworkConnector:
Updates the VPC configuration or operator role of an existing network connector. You can modify the subnet IDs, security group IDs, network protocol, or operator role. The connector must be in ACTIVE state to accept updates.

This operation is asynchronous. The connector remains in ACTIVE state during the update — existing workloads that reference this connector are not disrupted. Use GetNetworkConnector to monitor the LastUpdateStatus field, which transitions through InProgress to Successful or Failed. If the update fails, the LastUpdateStatusReasonCode field provides a specific error code for troubleshooting. This operation is idempotent when you provide a ClientToken.

Each successful configuration change creates a new immutable version. A connector can have a limited number of versions; once that limit is reached, further updates fail with NetworkConnectorLimitExceededException until you delete older versions.
operations.UpdateRuntime: Updates the properties of an existing customer-managed runtime, such as its description, license information, or lifecycle information.
operations.UpdateRuntimeAlias: Updates an existing runtime alias to point to a different runtime version or to change its description or lifecycle information.
operations.UpdateRuntimeVersion: Updates the runtime version release notes. The runtime version must be in the ACTIVE state. The runtime version image is immutable. To change the runtime contents, create a new runtime version.
